category: WS-L: Local Attack Surface — Custom Protocol Handler (heyclicky://)
item: Registry command registration (`"...\HeyClicky.exe" "%1"`), CLI argument parsing (`AppOptions.Parse`), and deep-link parsing (`AuthDeepLink.TryParse`)
notes: While `ProtocolRegistration.EnsureRegistered` quotes `"%1"` and `AppOptions.Parse` only recognizes `--background`/`--autostart`/`--launched-at-login`/`--reset-all` (preventing arbitrary CLI flag injection from a `heyclicky://` URL), `ProtocolRegistration.EnsureRegistered` overwrites `HKCU\Software\Classes\heyclicky\shell\open\command` with `Environment.ProcessPath` on every startup. Because the vendor `HeyClickyApp\current\HeyClicky.exe` also runs via `HKCU\...\Run\HeyClicky`, it overwrote the protocol handler away from `dist\kursor-desktop\HeyClicky.exe` (AUD-L-004).

category: WS-L: Local Attack Surface — Custom Protocol Handler (heyclicky://)
item: OAuth callback CSRF state guard (`SignInCallbackGuard.Evaluate`) and deep-link session overwrite (`SupabaseAuthService.TryCompleteSignInFromUrlAsync`)
notes: `SignInCallbackGuard.Evaluate` (`lines 60-65`) checks `if (isLocalSupabaseBackend) return Verdict.AcceptLocalDevelopment;` BEFORE verifying `pendingState` or `callbackState`. Any webpage triggering `heyclicky://auth-callback?access_token=...&referral_code=...` bypasses CSRF state validation, overwrites the local auth session (`AuthTokenStore`), and fires `ReferralCodeReceived` without an active sign-in flow (AUD-L-003).

category: WS-L: Local Attack Surface — Named Pipes, Shared Memory & Loopback Bridges
item: Single-instance mutex (`Local\HeyClicky-<SID>-primary-mutex`), 4096-byte Memory-Mapped File (`Local\HeyClicky-<SID>-primary`), and Named Pipe (`HeyClicky-<SID>-<PID>-<Guid>`) ACLs and argument deserialization
notes: `SingleInstance.cs:213-229` creates the MMF and `NamedPipeServerStream` with default ACLs (writable by any same-user local process) and shares the exact same mutex/MMF name with the vendor `HeyClicky.exe` binary (`AUD-L-004`). Additionally, `ReadActivationPayloadAsync` (`lines 368-408`) accepts up to 1 MB of newline-delimited arguments from any local process and forwards them to `ArgumentsReceived` without filtering internal flags (AUD-L-007).

category: WS-L: Local Attack Surface — Named Pipes, Shared Memory & Loopback Bridges
item: BrowserBridge Native Messaging Host (`ClickyBrowserBridge`) and Loopback MCP Server (`LoopbackMcpServer` / `LoopbackHttpServer`)
notes: `LoopbackHttpServer` binds strictly to `IPAddress.Loopback` (`127.0.0.1`) with a 1 MB header/body cap and `LoopbackMcpServer` enforces `CryptographicOperations.FixedTimeEquals` on `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. However, `ClickyBrowserBridge.WriteConnectionFile` (`lines 256-267`) writes `{"port":...,"token":"..."}` in plaintext to `%LOCALAPPDATA%\HeyClicky\BrowserBridge\connection.json` (verified live on port 51635: `200 OK` on `tools/list` using the disk token, AUD-L-006), and overwrites `HKCU\Software\Google\Chrome\NativeMessagingHosts\com.heyclicky.browser` with `BrowserHost\com.heyclicky.browser.json` pointing to whichever `HeyClicky.exe` started last (AUD-L-004).

category: WS-L: Local Attack Surface — Localhost Backend (:8787), OAuth Loopback (:48611) & Custom Connectors
item: Backend TCP binding address (`127.0.0.1:8787`), wildcard CORS (`Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *`), and zero-auth middleware (`clientHeadersAndAuthMiddleware`)
notes: While the backend binds to `127.0.0.1:8787`, `app.use("*", cors())` (`Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *`) combined with `clientHeadersAndAuthMiddleware` (which auto-authenticates unauthenticated requests as `DEFAULT_USER_ID`) allows any website visited in a browser to make cross-origin `fetch` calls to `http://127.0.0.1:8787` and exfiltrate master API keys (`GEMINI_API_KEY`, `DEEPGRAM_API_KEY`, `OPENAI_API_KEY` from `/v2/dictation/gemini-token`, `/deepgram/token`, `/realtime/token`), read/modify `/memory`, and read `/agent/integrations` (AUD-L-001). Additionally, `GET /auth/v1/authorize` (`auth.ts:100-121`) has an open redirect (`redirect_to`) that appends `access_token` and `refresh_token` to arbitrary external URLs (AUD-L-003).

category: WS-L: Local Attack Surface — Localhost Backend (:8787), OAuth Loopback (:48611) & Custom Connectors
notes: `gzipMiddleware` buffers the full compressed body and calls `gunzipSync(compressedBuffer)` synchronously on the main thread without `maxOutputLength` or compressed input size limits, enabling a single gzip decompression bomb request to freeze the event loop or crash the backend with OOM (AUD-L-002).

category: WS-L: Local Attack Surface — Localhost Backend (:8787), OAuth Loopback (:48611) & Custom Connectors
item: MCP OAuth PKCE loopback server (`McpOAuth.cs` / `LoopbackCallbackServer.cs` on `127.0.0.1:48611`) and `CustomConnectorStore` stdio command execution (`CommandResolver.cs`)
notes: `McpOAuth.AuthorizeAsync` generates a 32-byte CSPRNG `verifier` (S256 PKCE) and 16-byte CSPRNG `state`, validates `https://` endpoints (allowing `http://` only for loopback), binds `LoopbackCallbackServer` strictly to `IPAddress.Loopback` (`127.0.0.1:48611` with fallback to ephemeral loopback port) for the duration of the OAuth flow, and verifies `callback.State == text2`. `CustomConnectorStore` encrypts connector secrets via DPAPI (`ProtectedData.Protect` with `DataProtectionScope.CurrentUser` and entropy `HeyClicky.Connectors.v1`) and spawns user-configured stdio MCP commands with `UseShellExecute = false` and `ArgumentList`.

category: WS-L: Binary Signing, DLL Search-Order & Autostart Hygiene
item: Authenticode signatures in `dist/kursor-desktop/`, DLL search-order hygiene, and autostart scripts (`start-kursor-hidden.vbs`, `install-autostart.ps1`, `seed-local-auth.ps1`)
notes: In `dist/kursor-desktop/`, `HeyClicky.exe` retains a `Valid` Authenticode signature while all 7 rebuilt managed assemblies (`HeyClicky.dll`, `HeyClicky.Core.dll`, `HeyClicky.Platform.dll`, `HeyClicky.Agents.dll`, `HeyClicky.Drawing.dll`, `HeyClicky.Drawing3D.dll`, `HeyClicky.Contracts.dll`) are `NotSigned` (AUD-L-007). `install-autostart.ps1` registers BOTH `HKCU\...\Run\Kursor` AND `Startup\Kursor.lnk` alongside the vendor `HKCU\...\Run\HeyClicky` entry (AUD-L-004, AUD-M-003). `seed-local-auth.ps1` writes PascalCase keys to `endpoints.json` (ignored by case-sensitive `AppBundleConfiguration.ReadConfigured`) and writes plaintext tokens to `session.json` (AUD-L-005).

item: Full-screen JPEGs (`ScreenCaptureService`), microphone PCM/WAV (`WasapiMicrophoneCapture`), UIA page text & browser URLs (`UiaPageText`), clipboard contents (`TextInsertion`), dictated text (`DictationTranscriptArchive`), OneBrain threads, SQLite `kursor.db`, and telemetry/Sentry (`ClickyAnalytics`, `CrashReporting`)
notes: While `BrainSession.cs:931` strips screenshots (`WithoutScreenshots(thread)`) before saving `%LOCALAPPDATA%\HeyClicky\OneBrain\<userId>\threads\<id>.json`, the backend `ensureSessionAndThread` (`brain.ts:171-186`) persists the raw `incomingThread`—including full `data:image/jpeg;base64,...` screenshots—into SQLite `threads.messages_json` without stripping images or pruning rows (verified by PoC 4 in `security-pocs.json`: 50,605-byte base64 JPEG persisted in `threads.messages_json`, AUD-L-006). Dictated text and target app names are stored in plaintext JSONL under `%LOCALAPPDATA%\HeyClicky\DictationTranscripts\*.jsonl` for 14 days, and `Properties/AssemblyInfo.cs:15-17` retains production `HeyClicky.SentryDsn` (`SendDefaultPii = true`) and `HeyClicky.PostHogApiKey` (AUD-L-006).

item: Backend cold-start latency, idle/active memory/CPU/handle/thread baselines (`node.exe`, warm TTS `powershell.exe`, `HeyClicky.exe`), and endpoint latency percentiles (`/health`, `/plan`, `/brain/turn` live vs local fallback, `/v2/dictation/cleanup`, `/agent/realtime/speak`, `analyzeScreenLayout` 1280x720 JPEG)
notes: All latency baselines and process metrics were measured and recorded in `docs/audit/ws-lm/PERF_DATA.json`. While `/health`, `/plan`, `analyzeScreenLayout` (1280x720 JPEG), warm SAPI TTS (`/agent/realtime/speak`), and pure local-fallback `/brain/turn` meet latency targets, `/brain/turn` with `force_local_fallback: true` on a configured backend still awaits `tryCallUpstreamLlm` (1–3s) before checking `!body.force_local_fallback` (`brain.ts:1021-1045`, AUD-M-001), and `src/backend/src/index.ts:2` calls `dotenv.config({ override: true })` which overrides caller-supplied environment variables when `.env` is present in `cwd`.

category: WS-M: Sustained Stress, Soak & Resource Leak Testing
item: 215-turn `/brain/turn` stress/soak test (including 20 screenshot turns and 15 mid-stream SSE client disconnects), 40 `/v2/dictation/cleanup` calls, 10 `/agent/realtime/speak` calls, 30 proactive job polls, SQLite DB/WAL growth, and Node heap/handle tracking
notes: The backend survived 215 `/brain/turn` requests, 40 dictation cleanups, 10 TTS syntheses, and 30 proactive polls with 0 HTTP 500s. However, SQLite `sessions` and `threads` grow monotonically on every turn without any retention limit or scheduled WAL checkpoint (`kursor.db` + `-wal` reached ~10 MB on the live instance), `agents.ts` accumulates `proactiveJobs`, `proactiveCardStatuses`, `turnLeases`, and `calendarEvents` in unbounded in-memory `Map`s/arrays (AUD-M-002), and client SSE disconnects do not abort in-flight upstream LLM requests or guard `ReadableStreamDefaultController.enqueue`/`close` (AUD-M-001).

item: Killing warm PowerShell SAPI TTS daemon (`warmSynthProc`) mid-request and verifying automatic respawn on next `/agent/realtime/speak` call; backend unavailability handling; and `start-kursor.ps1` / autostart process management
notes: Killing the warm PowerShell TTS daemon (`warmSynthProc`) mid-request is handled gracefully by `voice.ts:345-410`: the in-flight request falls back to `synthesizeWinRtWav`/`generateSilenceWav` (`200 OK`, `audio/wav`) and the next `/agent/realtime/speak` call automatically spawns a new `powershell.exe` daemon PID. However, `install-autostart.ps1` registers duplicate startup triggers (`HKCU\...\Run\Kursor` + `Startup\Kursor.lnk`, AUD-M-003), `start-kursor.ps1:113` checks `Get-Process -Name "HeyClicky"` without checking `.Path` (colliding with vendor `HeyClickyApp`, AUD-L-004), and `worker.ts:7-8` and `AgentHarnessRunnerProcess.cs:75` hardcode developer paths (`C:\Users\ubaid\...` and `C:\Users\niles\...`, AUD-M-004).
